items.title: Overview
items.description: Health Assistant Bridge — a universal adapter integration for the self-hosted, open-source health records platform. Connect browser extensions and mobile apps to ingest scraped medical data from portals without open APIs, with AI-powered ontology mapping and TypeScript/Python SDKs.

items.title: Authentication & Security
items.description: How a bridge client authenticates. UUID-as-secret (default, for a trusted LAN self-hosted box) vs optional HMAC api_secret (recommended for internet-exposed instances) — the X-Api-Signature canonical form, replay window, and which endpoints are signed.

items.title: Client SDK Setup
items.description: Install and configure the official Python (sync + async) and TypeScript client SDKs. Constructor options, timeouts, retry/backoff, HMAC signing, and the signing helpers for building your own client.

items.title: API Reference
items.description: The three bridge endpoints fully documented: /status (connectivity + cursor + SDK versions), /map (AI ontology mapping), and /sync (push observations + examinations). Request/response schemas, the Universal Data Contract, cursor handling, and dedup rules.

items.title: AI Ontology Mapping
items.description: The /map workflow — when and why to map raw metric names before syncing. How the LLM resolves localized portal terms (Natrium, HCT) to standardized biomarker definitions, map_to_existing vs create_new, and coding systems.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.description: Diagnose a bridge client. Resolve signed-request rejections, skew-window failures, a stuck cursor, the SDK version-mismatch warning, 400/422 on a malformed payload, and how to reset the sync cursor from the UI.
